title: ESP32 suspected of knocking out the home WiFi
description:
On 2026-10-08 the bench board ran from 17:02 to 22:03 (Madrid time). From 20:15 it had repeated internet outages of up to 17 minutes (DNS Failed, start_ssl_client -1). Around 21:00 the whole home network failed (the projector stopped working) and recovered as soon as the board was unplugged. The user is sure the board caused it.

There are documented cases of an ESP32 taking down a router: https://esp32.com/viewtopic.php?p=44018. Espressif put it down to an incompatibility between its WiFi driver and that router's firmware.

Measures:
1. WiFi.setSleep(false) in wifi_connection.cpp. Done; pending flash.
2. Search for known problems with the user's router model (model still unknown).
3. If it happens again: move to Arduino-ESP32 3.x (IDF 5, newer WiFi driver), and save logs with pio device monitor -f log2file plus a timestamped ping.
notes:
Router: Sagemcom F@st 5366S, ISP Pepephone. Searches on 2026-10-09 found no documented case of an ESP32 knocking out this model. There are general complaints that the Pepephone Sagemcom routers drop the connection and need reboots, and a forum comment says ISP routers have little memory and lock up with many devices. Neither is confirmed for our case.
2026-10-11 ~15:36: second outage. Board on fw 0.1.1 (setSleep(false) in place), up ~6600 s, RSSI -67 to -75 dBm, start_ssl_client -1, other home devices also lost WiFi. User thinks it began when the WiFi projector was switched on; on 2026-10-09 the projector was also involved. Hypothesis (unproven): projector WiFi (screen mirroring / WiFi Direct on 2.4 GHz) plus the ESP32 at weak signal retrying at low rates saturates 2.4 GHz airtime. Test: projector on with board off; board on with projector off; both on.
2026-10-13 22:18 Madrid (4th day): projector switched on, projector lost network; board unplugged and projector recovered. Board serial (fw 0.1.2, uptime 40488 s): no [wifi] disconnected event, one start_ssl_client -1 at 20:18Z, upload retried 10 s later OK; RSSI -69..-77. So the board stayed associated and barely noticed; the projector is the one that breaks. Next hypothesis to check first: IP conflict (both devices on the same IP, e.g. projector with a static IP). Then the monitored test.
2026-10-15: cause found. Projector had static IP 192.168.1.128 inside the DHCP range; the router gave .128 to the Mac too (verified: Mac en0 = .128 while projector on .128; Mac lost connection, projector 'connected, no internet'). Projector switched to DHCP, got .154, both recovered immediately. The ESP32 was not the cause. Logged in docs/hardware-log.md. Pending: soak test with board and projector both on before closing.
close_reason: Cause was the projector's static IP inside the DHCP range, not the ESP32 (hardware-log 2026-10-15). Soak 12:20-15:33 after the fix: 170/170 uploads HTTP 200, no WiFi disconnects or SSL errors.

title: Phantom rain tip on the bench
description: On 2026-10-08 at 20:01 UTC the bench station counted one rain tip (0.2794 mm) with nobody touching the gauge. The network was failing at the time and the Mac may have gone to sleep or woken up. Possible causes: the bucket settling from near its balance point, or electrical noise on GPIO 33. Watch for more tips. If they repeat, look at the wiring and noise filtering on GPIO 33 before the station goes outside.
notes:
2026-10-08: 7 tips with nobody touching the gauge (Madrid time): 17:56, 20:15, 20:19, 20:24 (two), 20:35 and 22:01. Five fall at the start of the network outages. Hypothesis, unconfirmed: current spikes from the WiFi retries put noise on GPIO 33.
2026-10-09: the 4 tips of the day were made by hand by the user. They are not phantom tips.
2026-10-09 11:56-11:59 (Madrid): 67 tips in 4 minutes (25, 27, 11, 4) plus one at 11:42, with nobody touching the gauge. At the same time the anemometer counted pulses (gusts of 0.2-0.4 m/s) while its cups were still. Both reed inputs received pulses together, which points to electrical noise or a loose contact, not to the gauge. No water can make 27 tips a minute. Blocks the outdoor installation.
2026-10-10: Touching cables showed nothing. Not tied to reboots (only the ISR increments the counter). Plan: pulse-width filter (count on release if pin was low >= RAIN_MIN_LOW_MS, provisional 10 ms; other gauges close 50-135 ms) in lib/pulse_filter with native tests, plus pin state, too-short count and last low width in the bench [live] line to calibrate by tipping by hand.
2026-10-13: fw 0.1.1 (10 ms minimum) rejected real hand tips: each tip = 2 closures under 1 ms (millis resolution). fw 0.1.2: filter in microseconds (esp_timer_get_time), RAIN_MIN_LOW_US = 0 while measuring (counts like the plain 200 ms debounce, which merges the 2 closures), live log shows closures per 10 s and the longest in us. Next: compare hand-tip widths with phantom widths and set the minimum.
2026-10-13 fw 0.1.2 hand test: 5 tips counted 5 (ok). 11 closures for 5 tips. Longest closure per 10 s window: 14 us (one tip whose closures were all that short), 146 ms, 141 ms. Real closures range from ~14 us to ~146 ms, so a minimum-width filter would lose real tips: keep RAIN_MIN_LOW_US = 0. Next: capture a phantom tip's closures/longest with fw 0.1.2; candidate fix is a 100 nF capacitor GPIO 33-GND (reed closing discharges it at once, so short real closures survive; noise spikes get absorbed).
2026-10-15: soak 12:20-15:33 (fw 0.1.2, projector fixed): 0 tips, 0 closures, noise 0, 0 wind pulses. Phantom tips did not come back in 3 h. Still no phantom width to compare; keep watching on later runs before setting RAIN_MIN_LOW_US.
close_reason: No phantom tips since the final wiring: 0 in 3 h 24 min indoors, 1 h on the power supply and on the mast. The 2026-10-19 burst came from the expansion board's bad GND contact (board swapped, rain gauge on GPIO 26). Reopen if they come back.

title: API: cached read endpoints on Vercel (/api/now, /api/day, /api/month, /api/daily)
description: Read layer between the browser and Supabase. Vercel api/ routes in the frontend project read Supabase with the secret key (Vercel env vars only, never in client code). Fixed endpoints, no free queries: /api/now (latest), /api/day?date=YYYY-MM-DD, /api/month?month=YYYY-MM, /api/daily (all days since install, ~365 rows/year). Cache-Control s-maxage: 60 s for now/today/current month; long (hours/days) for closed days/months since the past never changes. Strict param validation (format, no unknown params, no future dates, none before install) and 400 otherwise, so bots cannot bust the cache with random query strings. Device chosen by env var (bench vs station). Optional later: Vercel firewall rate limit per IP (check what the free plan includes).

title: Post-install review of the first days on the mast
description: After going live on 2026-10-20 (15:50 Madrid): (1) review the first 24 h with pnpm station logs meteo-station-lasrozas-1 24: reboots or brownouts, WiFi drops (RSSI about -72 dBm on the mast), gaps, sun heating the shield; (2) compare the vane with Open-Meteo hour by hour over a few hours of steady wind and set VANE_OFFSET_DEG over OTA only if there is a steady offset; (3) note the installation in docs/hardware-log.md; (4) the user sets STATION_DEVICE_ID=meteo-station-lasrozas-1 in Vercel.
notes:
2026-10-21 morning check: 19 h up, 0 reboots, 0 gaps, RSSI -69 dBm, 3 single failed uploads (retried fine), no phantom rain. Suspect sun on the shield: between 10:16 and 10:21 Madrid the temperature jumped 12.3 -> 14.2 C in 5 min (RH 67.5 -> 62.1, as if the sensor heated), then stayed about 14.7 while Open-Meteo central Madrid said 11.0 C at 10:45. Check whether the step repeats at the same time on sunny mornings; if so, improve the shield placement or shade it.
2026-10-21: user confirms direct sun reaches the shield at that time. Passive TFA shield, so 1-3 C warm bias in strong sun with light wind is expected. Next: (a) check BME280 centered in the shield and not touching the plates, no dark roof/wall right below or beside it, ESP32 box not under the shield; (b) after a few days compare sunny vs cloudy mornings against Open-Meteo; if the bias is steady, mention it on the dashboard. Do not correct it with a formula (depends on wind and cloud). User is fine with it for now: it reflects their sunny spot.
2026-10-22 check: 1440/1440 readings on 10-21, none missing on 10-22 so far. Sun on the shield confirmed, same clock window both days: temperature steps up at about 10:18 Madrid and drops back at about 11:48 (10-21: 12.2 -> 14.1 at 10:20, 16.6 -> 14.3 at 11:50; 10-22: 10.1 -> 14.4 at 10:25, peak 20.8 at 11:42 vs about 15 after, Open-Meteo central Madrid 11.1-13.6). Sun then low in the south-east (azimuth about 125-145 deg, elevation about 22-31 deg). The fake peak became the 10-22 daily max (real max about 18 C late afternoon) and feeds the daily push correction through yesterday's measured max. Fix is physical: shade the shield from the low south-east sun or move it; the user should look at the mast around 10:30.

title: Ingest drops a whole reading when one field is out of range
description: ingest validates each field (rain_mm max 50, pressure 850-1100, ...) and skips the whole reading when one is out of range, only logging console.warn. On 2026-10-19 a wiring fault gave hundreds of phantom rain tips (over 50 mm a minute): those readings were dropped, losing temperature, humidity and wind too. Better: store the reading with the bad field as null (and log it as a device event), or cap/flag it in the firmware.

title: Firmware: OTA updates with rollback
description: Include OTA from first flash. When the ingest response names a new target version, download it over HTTPS (signed URL from meteo-gel), check its sha256, install it in the other OTA partition and reboot. Rollback: Arduino-ESP32 2.0.17 has CONFIG_APP_ROLLBACK_ENABLE; override verifyRollbackLater() and mark the new image valid only after its first delivered upload, otherwise roll back (about 10 min). Default partitions give 1.25 MB per app; firmware is 962 KB today.
notes:
2026-10-15 from meteo-gel: ingest 200 response may include update: {version, url (signed, 600 s), sha256, size} when devices.target_fw differs from the fw of the newest accepted reading. Firmware must remember a version that failed (rollback) and not retry it, or a broken target loops: rollback -> old fw -> offered again.
2026-10-15: code written, not built. lib/ota_policy (pure, 14 native tests pass with clang): parseUpdateOffer (ArduinoJson 7.4.3, filter on 'update'; semver, https, 64 lowercase hex, size>0), decideOffer (Install/AlreadyRunning/FailedBefore/WaitRetry 1 h), bootOutcome (Normal/Verifying/RolledBack from NVS 'installed' vs FW_VERSION), sha256Hex. src/net/ota_update: verifyRollbackLater() returns true (same as RainMaker lib); NVS namespace 'ota' keys installed/failed; download with HTTPClient + Update + mbedtls sha256, WDT reset per chunk, Update.end only if size and sha match; installs only with 0 pending readings and portal closed; mark valid on first delivered upload; esp_ota_mark_app_invalid_rollback_and_reboot after 10 min. Uploader passes the 200 body to otaOnDelivered. FW 0.3.0 (one USB flash: 0.2.0 has no OTA client). Test plan: publish 0.3.1 bench build; rollback test 0.3.2 built with a wrong INGEST_URL path.
2026-10-16: OTA 0.3.0 -> 0.3.1 works on the bench (download, sha256, reboot, kept). pnpm firmware publish/target/status replaces publish-firmware.ts; env in backend/.env.local. Migration grants update(target_fw) to service_role. Rollback test pending.
2026-10-16: rollback verified: 0.3.2 (wrong INGEST_URL) installed, no readings 09:25-09:34 UTC, back on 0.3.1 at 09:35 and not reinstalled while target stayed 0.3.2.
close_reason: OTA install and rollback verified on the bench (hardware-log 2026-10-16).

title: Push: forged subscriptions can fill the 1000 cap
description: Follow-up from the final review of feat/daily-forecast-push (M5). Only 404/410 delete a subscription, so subscriptions with valid-looking but forged endpoints/keys (accepted by api/push/subscribe within 10 req/h per IP) stay forever and can fill MAX_SUBSCRIPTIONS (1000). Do NOT delete on 403: a VAPID key change would wipe every real subscriber. Options: count consecutive failures per subscription and delete after N days failing; or delete rows never successfully sent to (last_sent_at null) after a week. Manual cleanup meanwhile: delete from push_subscriptions where last_sent_at is null and created_at < now() - interval '7 days';

title: Forecast: correct Open-Meteo's bias with the station's own data
description: Learn Open-Meteo's typical error at the station and correct the forecast shown on the dashboard (Predicción tab). Compare, hour by hour, what Open-Meteo forecast with what the station measured (temperature first, then humidity and wind), by time of day and forecast lead time, over a rolling window so it follows the seasons. Needs 2-4 weeks of readings from the mast (live since 2026-10-20). First check whether Open-Meteo's Previous Runs / Historical Forecast APIs give the forecasts as they were issued; if not, start storing our own forecast snapshots now so the history exists. Show the corrected values with the raw model available for comparison. Decided 2026-10-20: no Zambretti forecaster, Open-Meteo already covers it.
notes: 2026-10-20, asked by the user: enrich it with the same date in past years, when there is data. The station has none yet (live since 2026-10-20); until it has a year or more, use Open-Meteo's Historical Weather API (reanalysis archive, decades back) for the climatology of that calendar day (normal, min, max, typical range over a window of days around it). Uses: weigh the forecast toward the normal for long lead times, where the model's skill drops; and context on the dashboard (e.g. today is 3 °C above the normal for this date). Switch to the station's own past years as they accumulate, corrected for the bias between reanalysis and the station.

Ranges, all Europe/Madrid with DST: Hoy = 00:00 today to now (minute data, /api/day); 24 h = now-24h to now (minute data, new endpoint); 7 dias = 00:00 of today-6 to now (hourly aggregates).
